'''Matt Spaeth''' (born November 24, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]], where he was twice named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]], once a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]], and the 2006 winner of the [[John Mackey Award]].

He was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the third round of the [[2007 NFL draft]] and played seven seasons for them, becoming a [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl champion]] when the Steelers won [[Super Bowl XLIII]]. He also played two seasons for the [[Chicago Bears]].

'''Matthew Edward Turk''' (born June 16, 1968) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[punter (gridiron football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{cite web| url = http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-01-05/sports/fl-notre-dame-local-players-0106-20130105_1_matt-turk-long-snapper-ben-turk| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130702135849/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-01-05/sports/fl-notre-dame-local-players-0106-20130105_1_matt-turk-long-snapper-ben-turk| archive-date = 2013-07-02| title = Notre Dame's Cowart, Turk enjoy perfect homecoming - Sun Sentinel}}</ref> He was originally signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 1993. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Whitewater]]. A three-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection, Turk was also a member of the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Washington Redskins]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[New York Jets]], [[St. Louis Rams]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], and [[Houston Texans]]. '''John Matthew Stafford'''<ref name="Matthew Stafford - PFR">{{Cite web |title=Matthew Stafford Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StafMa00.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190407134229/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StafMa00.htm |archive-date=April 7, 2019 |access-date=August 6, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> (born February 7, 1988) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], receiving first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2008, and was selected [[List of first overall NFL draft picks|first overall]] by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the [[2009 NFL draft]]. Ranking in the top 10 of all time in pass attempts, pass completions, passing yards, and passing touchdowns, Stafford is currently sixth all time in passing yards per game and the fastest player in NFL history to have reached 40,000 career passing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Passing Yards per Game Career Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/pass_yds_per_g_career.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201117193438/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/pass_yds_per_g_career.htm |archive-date=November 17, 2020 |access-date=November 20, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

As the Lions' primary starter from 2009 to 2020, Stafford had a breakout year in 2011 when he became the fourth quarterback in NFL history to [[List of NFL quarterbacks with 5,000 passing yards in a season|throw for more than 5,000 yards]] in a single season, while also leading Detroit to their first playoff appearance since 1999. He helped the Lions reach the playoffs two more times in 2014 and 2016, earning [[Pro Bowl]] honors during the former and setting the NFL season record for comeback wins in the latter. After mutually agreeing to part ways with the Lions, Stafford was traded to the Rams in 2021 and led them to victory in [[Super Bowl LVI]]. In 2025, Stafford led the league in passing yards and touchdowns for the first time in his career, earning him [[Associated Press NFL Most Valuable Player Award|NFL Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Jackson |title=Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford wins NFL MVP |url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/rams-quarterback-matthew-stafford-wins-nfl-mvp |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=FoxNews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Matthew James Ulrich''' (December 30, 1981 – November 5, 2023) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive guard]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern Wildcats]]. He won [[Super Bowl XLI]] with the Colts during the 2006 season over the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Lenthang |first=Marlene |date=2023-11-09 |title=Matt Ulrich, former Colts Super Bowl champ, dies at 41 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/matt-ulrich-former-colts-super-bowl-champ-dies-41-rcna124371 |access-date=2025-10-04 |website=NBC News}}</ref>

Ulrich was named [[Northwestern University]] team captain in 2004 and earned All-Big Ten Honorable Mention. He was named National Strength and Conditioning All-American in 2004 and still holds many Northwestern weight room records including squat (715), bench press (475), and incline press (425). Ulrich graduated in 2000 from [[Streamwood High School]], where he won All-State and All-Midwest honors in [[High school football|football]] and also competed in the [[shot put]]. He was a three time Academic All-State in Illinois.

Ulrich was the co-founder of Dexa Fit,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dexafit.com|title=Transform Your Life|website=DexaFit}}</ref> and was director of operations and sports performance at Winning Edge Athletics in Chicago. He was also a director with Profitable Ideas Exchange,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://profitableideas.com/team/|title=Meet our Leadership Team - Profitable Ideas Exchange (PIE)|website=profitableideas.com}}</ref> where he led a team that convenes and facilitates peer-to-peer interactions of chief procurement officers, supply chain executives, chief marketing officers, chief tax officers and managing partners on behalf of a variety of clients including Accenture, KPMG, and Slalom Consulting.

'''Matthew Jerome Suhey''' (born July 7, 1958) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for ten seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Chicago Bears]]. He won a [[Super Bowl]] as a member of the [[1985 Chicago Bears season|1985 Bears]] while scoring a [[touchdown]] in the game and was named to the Pennsylvania Football All-Century Team.<ref>[http://www.pafootballnews.com/AllCenturyTeams.htm] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060218053707/http://www.pafootballnews.com/AllCenturyTeams.htm|date=February 18, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1986-01-27 |title=Bears Trounce Patriots, 46-10, in Super Bowl |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1986-01-27-mn-540-story.html |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

Before his NFL career, Suhey played [[college football]] at [[Penn State]] from 1976 to 1979, rushing for 2,818 yards and 26 touchdowns, while also catching 39 passes for 328 yards and 2 scores, along with 21 punt returns for 252 yards and another touchdown.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/matt-suhey-1.html | title=Matt Suhey College Stats }}</ref>

Suhey was the lead blocker and friend of [[Walter Payton]]. He is also a close friend of the Payton family, and the executor of the Payton estate since the death of Walter. Although Suhey was never a leader in any statistical category, he was a fan favorite for his personality and blocking ability.

Matt Suhey is one of three sons of [[College Football Hall of Fame]] [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] [[Steve Suhey]] to letter at Penn State University and a grandson of Hall of Fame Penn State player and coach [[Bob Higgins (American football)|Bob Higgins]]. His son, Joe Suhey, was a fullback at Penn State from 2007 to 2011. The Higgins–Suhey family is often referred to as the "first family of Penn State football" due to their affiliation with the program spanning four generations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statecollege.com/news/local-news/ginger-suhey-matriarch-of-penn-state-first-family-of-football-dies,942430/|title=Ginger Suhey, Matriarch of Penn State First Family of Football, Dies|date=2011-11-23|accessdate=2014-06-01|archive-date=2014-06-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605051610/http://www.statecollege.com/news/local-news/ginger-suhey-matriarch-of-penn-state-first-family-of-football-dies,942430/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
